Case PUR-2025-00057 — final order approving Appalachian Power revisions to the terms and conditions of Rate Schedule L.P.S.
The SCC adopted the Hearing Examiner's report in full and approved APCo's revised Schedule L.P.S. special terms and conditions for large load customers

New or expanded load at or above 100 MW at a single site, or 150 MW aggregated, in APCo territory after 1 July 2025 now faces a 14-year initial term inclusive of up to a four-year ramp, 80% monthly minimum billing demand, cash collateral with no freely negotiated alternative, 42 months' notice to terminate or cut capacity beyond 20%, and an exit fee. A separate large-load rate class was expressly found not to be required.
Final order entered; revised tariff sheets acknowledged 2026-07-13
APCo to file Schedules O.A.D. and F.O.A.D. revisions with its next biennial review
Docket 26-0000114 — PNM certificate and purchased-power applications for 2029-2032 resources
PNM seeks approval for 2029-2032 resources alongside abandonment of Four Corners
Determines whether PNM has generation and storage capacity to serve new large load after the 2029 Four Corners retirement — it bounds interconnection headroom for any New Mexico siting decision.
Docket 2026-138-E — petition to establish a generic docket for comments addressing large load additions
Duke Energy Carolinas and Duke Energy Progress petitioned the South Carolina PSC to open a generic docket on large load additions

The single venue where South Carolina's rules for interconnecting and serving very large loads are being written. Google, Dominion Energy South Carolina, Nucor and the Office of Regulatory Staff are all parties, so the terms set here will govern data-centre service conditions statewide.
Docket 2026-138-E — Duke petition for a generic large-load proceeding in South Carolina
Duke Energy Carolinas and Duke Energy Progress petition to open a generic docket on new large-load additions at 50 MW and above
Will set how large loads are priced and cost-allocated in Duke's South Carolina territory. Google is among the intervenors. Sourced from search snippets, not the docket page.
Docket E-01345A-25-0105 — APS rate case with XHLF revisions
APS rate case hearing opens, including revisions reallocating cost to high-load-factor data-centre customers

A reported 45%-plus increase aimed specifically at the XHLF data-centre class within a roughly 14% overall request. Direct pricing risk for any APS data-centre counterparty. Figures from secondary reporting, not the primary filing.
Docket 55378 / 56002 — Georgia Power Q1 2026 Quarterly Large Load Economic Development Report
Georgia Power reports 12,400 MW committed across 31 customers against a 76,200 MW pipeline

The richest recurring disclosure in the coverage set. Commitments have grown from 3,600 MW at the 2023 IRP update to 12,400 MW, of which 8,500 MW has broken ground. Pipeline churn is itemised: 12,600 MW entered, 2,900 MW exited.
Docket U-37882 — LPSC takes original jurisdiction over the Entergy Lightning Directive application
LPSC votes 4-1 to take original jurisdiction and sets certification of roughly 5,200 MW of gas generation for 16 December 2026
Fixes the exact date the LPSC will vote on certifying the generation build serving Meta's Richland Parish site — the single hardest dated decision point in the tracker.
LPSC Business and Executive Session vote
GRDA board of directors agenda, 13 May 2026 — item V.J, Schedule WP-SS wholesale full requirements service supplemental supply and large load rider
GRDA's board took up a Schedule WP-SS supplemental supply and large load rider for wholesale full requirements service

GRDA is building a dedicated large-load rate construct on the wholesale full-requirements side, the mechanism that would price incremental data-centre load served through its municipal and cooperative customers. Rider terms are not in the agenda.
Board action item; rider text not published
GRDA board of directors agenda, 13 May 2026 — item IV.C.11, amendment to the Exhibit B schedule of the Large General Service Industrial agreement with Google LLC
GRDA's board took up a contract amendment updating the Exhibit B schedule to its Large General Service Industrial agreement with Google

Direct confirmation that a hyperscaler is under contract on the GRDA system as a named Large General Service Industrial customer, and that its service schedule was being amended in May 2026. No MW figure, price or term is disclosed in the agenda.
Board action item; amendment scope not published
Case PUR-2026-00011 — interim order establishing additional proceedings on the large-load queue standards
The Commission ordered jointly revised queue standards, briefing on the legal impediments to a fast-track interconnection queue, and a study of voluntary load flexibility for large load customers

The SCC signalled it will require a public anonymised interconnection-request database refreshed at least twice a year, published study timelines with justification for delay, and a transition plan for queued projects. It also floated letting a large-load customer buy queue priority through multi-year contributions offsetting Dominion's demand-side management revenue requirement, which is speed-to-power traded for load-flexibility funding.
Parties did not fully agree; briefs filed 2026-06-30; decision pending
Commission order on standards, fast-track and load flexibility
Docket M-2025-3054271 — Pennsylvania PUC large-load model tariff framework
Pennsylvania PUC issues a first-of-its-kind statewide model tariff framework for large-load customers

Sets the cost-causation, collateral, exit-fee and six-month interconnection-study rules that will govern every future Pennsylvania large-load interconnection. Thresholds are 50 MW for a single customer or 100 MW aggregate.
Docket ER26-1731 — SPP Attachment Z1 revisions
SPP allows long-term transmission service to be pursued simultaneously with generator interconnection, capped at the injection limit per point of interconnection
A technical change that matters for structuring co-located load-plus-generation: it prevents overselling capacity at a single point of interconnection.
PPL advanced-stage load 28.3 GW; ~10 GW under ESAs with 5 GW under construction
Kentucky data-centre queue nearly doubles from 8.2 to 11.9 GW. PPL also announces an X-energy collaboration on advanced nuclear in Kentucky explicitly to support large-load growth.
Evergy signs a fifth ESA with an unnamed BBB+ developer; Tier 1 signed load reaches ~3.0 GW
Load growth CAGR raised from ~6% to ~7-8%. Evergy also amended two of the original four ESAs to improve 2026 margins — a reminder that signed does not mean static.

Ameren Q1 2026 earnings conference call presentation
Ameren reiterated 2.2 GW of executed Missouri ESAs and an unchanged 3.4 GW construction-agreement funnel, with no incremental ESA execution in the quarter

A flat quarter: zero net ESA conversion, with the February figures repeated verbatim. The +0.6 GW step to the Q2 2026 figure of 2.8 GW therefore all occurred in Q2 rather than spread across the half. Ameren expects to request roughly 3 GW of new resources from the MoPSC by Q3 2026.
TEP's first data-centre ESA at 300 MW is projected to save a typical residential customer ~US$13 per month
A rare quantified ratepayer benefit from a single large-load contract. A second site is in negotiation, and transmission work is underway at Big Cedar to serve a further 1,600 MW by 2028.
Dominion Energy Q1 2026 earnings call slides
As of March 2026 Dominion's ladder stood at SELOA 29.5 GW, CLOA 11.1 GW and ESA 10.4 GW, about 51.0 GW in total and up 5% on December

A weak conversion quarter at the signed end: ESA advanced only +0.2 GW and CLOA +0.1 GW, while essentially all of the 2.5 GW quarterly gain landed in the earliest SELOA engineering stage. The heavy ESA conversion came instead in Q2 2026, +1.6 GW to 12.0, drawn largely out of CLOA.
Docket 24-0854-E-42T — Appalachian Power and Wheeling Power Rule 42T base rate case
The Commission's case register shows the Appalachian Power and Wheeling Power Rule 42T general rate case reaching final disposition

The base rate proceeding that sets the cost-allocation framework and rate schedules applying to Appalachian Power's West Virginia industrial and large-capacity customers, so the reference point for any large-load pricing negotiated in the state. The substantive outcome was not read.
Docket PUD2026-000031 — OG&E application for pre-approval of a special contract (caption unconfirmed — OCC WebLink search returning HTTP 500)
OG&E files for pre-approval of a special contract, relief type Contract - Special

Timing and relief type match the widely reported OG&E large-load contract tied to Google. If confirmed it sets the counterparty pricing precedent for Oklahoma. The counterparty is NOT confirmed — only index metadata was read, not the filing itself.
Docket 26-0000091 — PNM Rider 45E economic development contract, Castelion Corporation
PNM files an original Rider 45E special economic-development contract with a named counterparty
Confirms PNM is actively executing negotiated large-customer contracts — a live template for future large-load special contracts in a territory where no large-load tariff yet exists.
CAISO Extended Day-Ahead Market goes live with PacifiCorp
EDAM launches; PNM has a signed implementation agreement to join in 2027

PNM's EDAM entry is now confirmed by signed agreement rather than intent, setting a firm clock for market-design and counterparty exposure. EDAM is expected to cover roughly 42% of Western electricity demand once 2027 joiners are active.

Entergy Q1 2026 earnings presentation — docket U-37882
Entergy signs Meta ESA in north Louisiana, with 7 CCGTs exceeding 5,200 MW and $12.9B committed to serve it

Capital plan jumps $14B to $57B in a single quarter, almost entirely to serve one named counterparty. The largest single-customer generation commitment in the coverage set, plus up to 2,500 MW of renewables under the Louisiana green tariff.
Louisiana PSC review of docket U-37882
MISO clears roughly 142.6 GW of summer capacity, 3.5 points above its 7.9% reserve-margin target

In contrast to PJM's shortfalls, MISO currently shows headroom for near-term large-load additions. Figures rely on a search cache rather than a direct fetch of the MISO release, so confidence is capped.
OG&E names Google as the previously unnamed IRP Customer X, with three data centres in Stillwater and Muskogee
The counterparty behind Oklahoma's generation need is now public. MW not disclosed. A special-contract filing followed within days.
Docket 26-0364 — ICC own-motion investigation into ComEd large-load ratepayer protections
ICC opens an own-motion investigation into ratepayer protections and cost recovery for ComEd large-demand customers

The follow-on proceeding that decides whether Riders NS, ZSS and DE and the LDPAC deposit framework get restructured. Any Illinois pricing decided before it resolves carries regulatory-change risk. Status is Hearing Pending.
Virginia legislation creates and amends the Dominion GS-5 large-load rate class and allows direct assignment of PJM capacity costs

If signed as passed, the most direct statutory large-load cost-allocation mechanism in the mid-Atlantic, materially affecting Dominion siting economics. Final gubernatorial action was not confirmed in this pass.
Passed both chambers; final signature unconfirmed

Docket E-01773A-26-0123 — joint application for a streamlined process for multiparty agreements for electric service to large-load customers
Arizona Electric Power Cooperative and five distribution cooperatives applied for a streamlined process for multiparty large-load service agreements; Decision No. 82128 issued 2026-08-27

Creates a defined route for a large load sited in Arizona cooperative territory to be served under a single multiparty agreement spanning the generation-and-transmission cooperative and the distribution cooperative, materially faster than a bespoke special-contract proceeding.
Decision No. 82128 issued; compliance filing made 2026-09-10
Kansas extends the parallel-generation exclusion keeping large-load demand out of the export-capacity calculation
A narrow but real co-location enabler for behind-the-meter generation serving large loads in Evergy's Kansas territory.
PUCT Project 58777 — ERCOT preliminary Long-Term Load Forecast 2026-2032
ERCOT projects roughly 367,790 MW of demand by 2032 against an all-time peak of 85,508 MW
More than a fourfold increase over the record peak, driven by data centres, crypto and industrial load. Any procurement or siting assumption keyed to ERCOT's prior forecasts needs recalibrating.
Docket 26-0000071 — application for a CCN for a replacement 200 MW Eddy high voltage direct current tie
EPE applied for a certificate to build a replacement 200 MW Eddy HVDC tie
The Eddy tie is EPE's bridge to the Eastern Interconnection, so a replacement 200 MW DC tie governs how much external supply EPE can import to serve incremental southern New Mexico load.
Docket E-100 Sub 190 — Duke semi-annual report on large-load customers in advanced development
Duke reports 38 advanced-development projects totalling 5,610 MW, of which 16 projects and 4,332 MW are under executed ESAs

The clearest split anywhere between real and speculative data-centre demand on Duke's system — a 77% execution rate by MW, up roughly 2,330 MW on the Fall 2025 report. Figures were read from a rendered page image, not machine-extracted, and the sub-docket number needs confirmation.
GRDA board of directors agenda, 8 April 2026 — item 4.c, transmission study cost agreement with Cattle Run Land LLC
GRDA's board took up a transmission study cost agreement with Cattle Run Land LLC alongside similar agreements with two municipal authorities

A transmission study cost agreement with a private land-holding company rather than a municipal customer is the earliest public marker of a non-utility party testing deliverability on the GRDA system. The agenda does not state load type, size or end use.
Board action item; purpose not stated
Study results or a service agreement
Docket 59611 — El Paso Electric Schedule 27 High Load Factor Large Power Service
EPE applies for a high-load-factor large-power-service tariff, contested by the City of El Paso
Creates a new large-customer rate class in EPE's Texas territory. The outcome sets the rate structure and effective date.
Case PUR-2026-00044 — Appalachian Power Company application for an increase in base rates
Appalachian Power has a contested base rate increase pending, with Staff testimony filed 2026-09-16 and an evidentiary hearing set for 20 October 2026

The proceeding in which APCo's class cost of service and the price level under Schedule L.P.S. will be reset, following the June 2026 order that added large-load special terms but changed no rates. The application itself was not opened, so its treatment of large-load cost allocation is not established.
Georgia data-centre ratepayer-protection bill passes the House 159-5 then dies at adjournment
Failure leaves cost-shift protection resting on the Georgia PSC's March 2026 rule alone — a commission rule is more easily reversed than a statute.
Docket 25-0392-EL-AIR — AEP Ohio distribution rate case stipulation adopted
PUCO adopts the joint stipulation resetting AEP Ohio distribution rates

Resets the base distribution cost structure against which Schedule DCT and other large-load riders are layered. The Ohio Manufacturers' Association Energy Group participated, showing the data-centre fight spilling into general rate cases.
BHE 2026 investor presentation — Sierra Pacific generation
Sierra Pacific contracts Libra Solar at 700 MW plus 700 MW of storage, and Corsac 2 geothermal at 115 MW
Valmy peaking at 400 MW of gas remains under evaluation for May 2028. Northern Nevada supply is being built largely on contracted renewables and geothermal rather than gas.
NV Energy forecasts 3,600 MW of peak data-centre load by 2030 against ~400 MW in 2025

A ninefold increase, and the first NV Energy-specific pipeline figure available. NV Energy requires advances for distribution and transmission investment and plans to propose charges for incremental generation before rate-base inclusion. BHE group-wide has ~11,000 MW contracted.
Docket 26-0000062 — El Paso Electric Advice Notice No. 317, original Rate No. 50 High Load Factor Power Service
EPE filed a new Rate No. 50 High Load Factor Power Service open only to customers at or above 30 MW with monthly load factor at or above 85%

EPE New Mexico's first purpose-built large-load tariff and the schedule a Dona Ana or Santa Teresa data centre would take: 30 MW entry, transmission-voltage service into a dedicated substation, a 20-year minimum ESA term, a ramp capped at four years, billing demand floored at 80% of contract capacity plus an 80% summer ratchet, and credit security unless the offtaker holds two of three A-/A3 ratings.
Suspended 2026-04-24, extended 2026-08-28; motion for reconsideration filed 2026-09-08
Commission ruling on suspension; tied to rate case 25-00082-UT
West Virginia authorises microgrid districts letting certified data centres at 50 MW and above island behind the meter

The most permissive regime in the coverage set: qualifying large loads can bypass standard utility interconnection and cost allocation entirely, consuming 70%+ on site and selling up to 10% wholesale.
ISO-NE final draft 2026 Large Load Forecast
ISO-NE formalises a data-centre derating methodology that can cut a stated nameplate to 35-50% of reported MW

A template other regions may adopt or contest as their own forecasts mature. New England itself has only a couple of hundred MW of large load in formal study — far less pressure than CAISO, NYISO, PJM or ERCOT.
